title.value: Run Google Ads and Analytics tasks with an agent

introduction.value: A marketing agency tested ChatGPT Operator: it copied GA data into a Sheet with a chart and exported the search query report, but was slow and got stuck on a later step.

method.value: Alex Swerdlow tested OpenAI's Operator, a browser agent in the ChatGPT Pro plan, over three days. He had it log into Google Ads and Google Analytics. It copied GA data into a Google Sheet and charted it. It also found and exported the search query report, added a relevance column, and crawled a website. He took over to fix the Sheets mistakes.

outcome.value: The GA copy and chart mostly worked, with some formatting and data errors. After his manual fix, it scored about 30 query rows reasonably well, then crashed in a Sheets loop he couldn't clear. Day 1 failed completely.

notes.value: Day 1 took an hour or more and ended with a bare refusal. Responsiveness improved by day 2, but the author calls it a proof of concept, not ready for real work.

source_text.body:
Run Google Ads and Analytics tasks with an agent
A marketing agency tested ChatGPT Operator: it copied GA data into a Sheet with a chart and exported the search query report, but was slow and got stuck on a later step.
Done with
OP
Operator
What they did
Alex Swerdlow tested OpenAI's Operator, a browser agent in the ChatGPT Pro plan, over three days. He had it log into Google Ads and Google Analytics. It copied GA data into a Google Sheet and charted it. It also found and exported the search query report, added a relevance column, and crawled a website. He took over to fix the Sheets mistakes.
How it went
The GA copy and chart mostly worked, with some formatting and data errors. After his manual fix, it scored about 30 query rows reasonably well, then crashed in a Sheets loop he couldn't clear. Day 1 failed completely.
Worth knowing
Day 1 took an hour or more and ended with a bare refusal. Responsiveness improved by day 2, but the author calls it a proof of concept, not ready for real work.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
Open my Google Analytics property [property name] and copy the [metric, e.g. sessions by channel] for [date range] into a new Google Sheet, then add a chart of it. Next, go to Google Ads account [account name] and export the search query report for the same dates into the Sheet. Stop when the Sheet has both the chart and the report, and tell me if you get stuck on any step. Pause and ask me before changing any settings in either account.
Original source: https://openmoves.com/blog/testing-chatgpt-operator-for-google-ads-tasks/
